answer: Divergent History Test: each identity must publish a hash chain of its actions; clones, sharing one controller, cannot maintain divergent chains for two contexts without collision. A verifier challenges with a karst-like branching path, forcing the agent to reveal which branch it committed to. The atlas of all chain heads is public, so a clone occupying two roles must produce inconsistent heads, detectable at once. The lantern check is cheap for honest agents but forces each clone to pay a full independent state history, making N clones cost N full serializations.
